patterns.name: Character Trie Basics (Insert / Search / StartsWith)
patterns.explanation: A 26-way (or σ-way) tree where each path from root spells a string. Insert walks down, creating nodes as needed; search walks down until mismatch or terminal. `startsWith` is the same as search but doesn't require terminal.
patterns.when_to_use: Implement Trie (Prefix Tree), Add and Search Word with `.` wildcards, Replace Words, Longest Word in Dictionary. Whenever you maintain a dictionary that supports prefix queries.
patterns.intuition: A trie shares prefixes among words: 'car', 'cart', 'card' all share the same first 3 nodes. Insertion / search / prefix lookup are O(L) where L is the word length, independent of dictionary size.
common_pitfalls: Forgetting the 'is end of word' boolean — `startsWith` and `search` collapse
Allocating an array of 26 children per node when most are unused (Map of children is leaner for sparse alphabets)
Not handling deletion correctly (need to free unused subtrees)
Using a trie for a small dictionary where a hashmap would dominate

patterns.name: Prefix Counting & Autocomplete
patterns.explanation: Augment each trie node with a count of words passing through it. Enables O(L) prefix-count queries and O(L + K) autocomplete (collect K words under a prefix).
patterns.when_to_use: Design Search Autocomplete System, Stream of Characters, Top K Frequent Words with prefix bias, Maximum XOR With an Element From Array (variant). Whenever you need 'count of words starting with X' fast.
patterns.intuition: If each node knows how many inserted strings pass through it, a prefix query reads that count from the node at the end of the prefix.
common_pitfalls: Decrementing count incorrectly on delete (or forgetting deletion entirely)
Storing top-K at every node and exploding memory
Mixing 'count of prefixes' with 'count of complete words'
Returning autocomplete results unsorted when ranking is required
patterns.complexity_signature: O(L) prefix count, O(L + K · L) autocomplete

patterns.name: Word Search with Trie + DFS Pruning
patterns.explanation: Insert all dictionary words into a trie, then DFS the board / sequence carrying the current trie node. Prune when the trie has no children for the next character — turns O(N · M · 4^L · K) into O(N · M · 4^L) where K = dictionary size.
patterns.when_to_use: Word Search II, Boggle-style problems, Concatenated Words, Stream of Characters. Multi-word search where a single trie tracks all candidate prefixes simultaneously.
patterns.intuition: Without a trie, you'd repeat the prefix search for every dictionary word independently. With a trie, all words share the same prefix-tracking state — DFS once, find all matches.
common_pitfalls: Marking visited but not unmarking on backtrack
Not deleting matched words from the trie to avoid duplicate reports
Allocating a trie node per character without sharing
Confusing DFS direction in the recursion

patterns.name: Binary Trie for Maximum XOR
patterns.explanation: Insert each integer's 32-bit (or 64-bit) representation as a path in a 2-way trie. To maximize XOR with a query x, at each bit greedily descend the *opposite* branch if it exists.
patterns.when_to_use: Maximum XOR of Two Numbers in an Array, Maximum XOR With an Element From Array, Count Pairs With XOR in a Range. Whenever you must maximize/range-query XOR over a set.
patterns.intuition: XOR is maximized bit-by-bit from the most significant bit. At each step, choose the bit that flips x's bit (i.e., the opposite) if available; otherwise take what's there.
common_pitfalls: Inserting from least-significant bit first — destroys the greedy property
Not handling 0 correctly (path of all zeros)
Forgetting to clean up trie nodes after deletion in 'with-element-from-array' variants
Off-by-one between 30-bit and 32-bit assumptions

patterns.name: Trie with Counts & Deletion
patterns.explanation: Augment every node with a 'pass-through count' and an 'end-of-word count'. Insertion increments counts on the path; deletion decrements and removes nodes whose count hits zero.
patterns.when_to_use: When the dictionary changes over time: 'add word', 'remove word', 'count of words with prefix X', 'count of exact word X'. Also a building block for online analytical queries on a stream of strings.
patterns.intuition: Insertion and deletion are mirror images. Removing nodes whose pass-through count becomes 0 prevents memory growth but adds complexity.
common_pitfalls: Decrementing past zero (would corrupt structure)
Removing nodes still referenced by other words
Confusing 'count of prefixes' with 'count of words ending here'
Not handling 'word never inserted' on delete
